analysis:
The only change in this PR is documentation in docs/reference/configuration.md. It adds two table rows (head lines 316-317) for DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CHAINED and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CARRY. Both are env kill-switches that default on for Qwen inline-MTP scheduling and prefill-carry seeding in MTPContractsV2.swift. Both are documented as not forwarded to LaunchAgents.

No code, auth, attestation, crypto, coordinator-protocol or storage behavior changes in the supplied evidence. The rows do not touch any of the following: TB-002 (coordinator-to-provider WebSocket), the A-016 serving-authorization boundary, T-041 (prefix-cache salt and SSD tier), or TB-011 (App Attest authorization). The knobs are local, process-start, operator-controlled scheduling and performance toggles. They are documented as not widening admission or changing the privacy boundary.

The operator is already the adversary for the local process under TB-003. These variables give no new capability to coordinator or consumer adversaries. They are also not forwarded into launchd, so they do not alter installed-daemon behavior.

Unverified contract: the actual implementation in the libs/mlx-swift-lm MTPContractsV2.swift file is not in the supplied batch. I cannot confirm that the described behavior matches the code. In particular, I cannot confirm that carrying the prefill final-row hidden state or running ordinary chained decode preserves per-request isolation and does not leak state across requests (compare T-028). This is a documentation-only change, so I record the gap rather than a finding. Whichever PR carries the Swift implementation should be reviewed for cross-request state isolation.

The patch excerpt is truncated, but the range map is complete (head 316-317 only). Nothing indicates any other edits.
